batch_notes: Two very different shapes in this batch. The Rust targets (ycrdt, zip) are many small single-assertion properties that classify cleanly. The four TypeScript targets each have only 3-4 large 'omnibus' properties (one round trip over a whole option matrix, one oracle, one normal-form/consistency check) that internally classify inputs into known bug 'shapes' and count rather than fail; each of those targets then carries 12-16 example pins, one per bug, with no explicit link from pin to property. Consequently almost all attribution here is inferred, and the 'property' that found 10+ bugs is the single big round-trip test. The rubric has no place for the shape-gating pattern itself (a property that is simultaneously a discovery test and a regression-suppression list); it might deserve a tag. Quality notes: shell-quote pin comments cite bug ids as 'quote/N' while the bug records are 'shell-quote/N'; semver/6, /10 and /12 have property: null in their records even though the property bodies cite them and bugs_direct/mentioned_by link them, so those were reported as explicit. CRDT convergence tests (3 in ycrdt) were put under algebraic-law with tag stateful following batches 13 and 19; they are single-threaded simulations, not concurrency. TestHegelParseIsANormalForm (qs) and TestHegelDecodeIsStable (ini) are 'parse output is a normal form' properties that straddle spec-postcondition and roundtrip; I chose by the leading assertions of each.
